questions.q: What does 'phased recovery' mean in this lesson?
options: Bringing systems back into production in priority-ordered groups, with monitoring between each phase, instead of restoring everything at once
Restoring every system simultaneously the moment validation passes
Recovering only the most recently compromised system and leaving the rest offline indefinitely
A recovery method that skips validation entirely to save time
questions.explain: Phased recovery brings systems back in priority order with pauses to confirm nothing's wrong, rather than all at once.

questions.q: In Meridian's recovery plan, why did Tier 1 (domain controllers and core infrastructure) come back online before Tier 2 (the billing database server and RD Gateway)?
options: Tier 1 systems had already passed full validation with no findings and the rest of the environment depends on them, so a clean Tier 1 phase provides confidence before riskier systems return
Tier 1 systems were never actually part of the original incident
Tier 2 systems could not be validated at all
Tier order was decided randomly with no business or technical reasoning
questions.explain: Tiers are ordered by business criticality and validation confidence, with each clean phase justifying the next.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the specific signals Meridian's SOC watches for between recovery phases?
options: The reappearance of the same indicators of compromise from the original incident, such as the same scheduled task name or account name
A decrease in overall network bandwidth usage company-wide
The number of help desk tickets submitted that week
Whether the weather affects power and internet availability
questions.explain: Recurrence of the same IOCs from the original incident is a direct signal that reinfection may be underway.

questions.q: What is the main risk of bringing every recovered system back online simultaneously instead of in phases, according to this lesson?
options: If validation missed something on any single system, a full simultaneous restore makes that gap live across the entire environment at once, with no earlier signal to catch it
Simultaneous restores always take longer than phased ones
Systems cannot be validated at all unless they are restored one at a time
There is no real risk difference between phased and simultaneous recovery
questions.explain: Validation is a confidence level, not a guarantee; phasing limits the blast radius if that confidence turns out to be wrong somewhere.

questions.q: What does 'blast radius' refer to in the context of this lesson?
options: The scope of systems exposed if a validation gap turns out to be real, which phased recovery limits compared to restoring everything at once
The physical distance malware can travel between buildings
The total storage space used by an organization's backups
The number of employees affected by a company-wide email outage
questions.explain: Blast radius describes how far a missed validation gap can spread — phasing keeps that scope small instead of environment-wide.
